Habitat upstream of each crossing, per species

Source: R/lnk_aggregate.R
lnk_aggregate.Rd

For each crossing, sums the habitat of each species found anywhere upstream of it on the stream network: the crossing's own stream above it and every tributary, in every watershed group the persist schema holds. This is the demand side of prioritization: severity says how bad a barrier is, upstream habitat says what fixing it would open.

Usage

lnk_aggregate(
  conn,
  crossings,
  schema,
  to,
  config,
  species = NULL,
  col_id = "aggregated_crossings_id",
  barriers = NULL,
  barriers_col_id = "barriers_anthropogenic_id",
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

conn

A DBI::DBIConnection object.

crossings

Character. Schema-qualified table of crossings, with col_id, blue_line_key and downstream_route_measure. Typically a working schema's crossings.

schema

Character. The persist schema holding streams and streams_habitat_<sp> (for example "fresh_default"). Every group it holds is read: upstream habitat crosses watershed groups, so groups upstream of the crossings must be persisted for their habitat to count.

to

Character. <schema>.<table> to write (dropped and recreated), outside schema and different from crossings and barriers. One row per crossing and species.

config

Character. The config whose build schema holds, written to the config column (for example cfg$name).

species

Character vector of species codes, or NULL (default) for every streams_habitat_<sp> table in schema.

col_id

Character. Crossing identifier column. Default "aggregated_crossings_id".

barriers

Character or NULL. Schema-qualified table of human-made barriers (for example a working schema's barriers_anthropogenic, from lnk_barriers_emit()), with barriers_col_id, blue_line_key, downstream_route_measure. When given, each metric also gets a _belowupstrbarriers_km total: the habitat upstream of the crossing but below the next barriers upstream, as bcfishpass's *_belowupstrbarriers_km.

barriers_col_id

Character. Identifier column of barriers. Default "barriers_anthropogenic_id". Ids shared with crossings name the same feature.

verbose

Logical. Report each species' summary.

Value

invisible(to). Side effect: creates to.

Details

The walk is fresh::frs_aggregate(), refined by the measure-aware fwa_upstream(..., include_equivalents = TRUE, tolerance = 1) that bcfishpass's crossings_upstream_habitat uses, so a segment counts when it starts at or above the crossing (within 1 m) on the crossing's own stream, or lies on a stream that joins above it. The main stem below the crossing never counts.

Columns of to: the crossing id (named as col_id), config, species_code, then in km:

  • spawning_km: segments the species spawns on;

  • rearing_km: segments it rears on, lake connection lines left out, as lnk_rollup_wsg()'s rearing_km;

  • rearing_stream_km, rearing_lake_km, rearing_wetland_km: that rearing split by the polygon each line sits in;

  • rearing_lake_connection_km: rearing on lake connection lines (FWA edge 1450 in a lake), which bcfishpass counts in rearing.

Each sum is exact (numeric), so it does not depend on row order. A crossing with no habitat upstream gets zeros. A crossing whose measure is exactly the top of its stream has no segment holding it, so nothing is found above it and it gets zeros.

The barrier totals subtract, from a crossing's total, the totals of the barriers upstream of it that have no other barrier between it and them (a barrier at the crossing's own id is not its own upstream barrier). Of two barriers within 1 m on one stream, the one with the higher measure is upstream of the other, so the habitat above the pair is subtracted once.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
conn <- lnk_db_conn()
# a working schema left by lnk_pipeline_run(cleanup_working = FALSE)
lnk_aggregate(conn,
  crossings = "working_adms.crossings",
  schema = "fresh_default",
  to = "working_adms.crossings_upstream_habitat",
  config = "default",
  barriers = "working_adms.barriers_anthropogenic")

# which barriers block the most chinook spawning below the next barrier?
DBI::dbGetQuery(conn, "
  SELECT aggregated_crossings_id, spawning_belowupstrbarriers_km
  FROM working_adms.crossings_upstream_habitat
  WHERE species_code = 'CH'
  ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 5")
} # }
